summary: kb repair — finds notes that are written but UNFINDABLE and hands them to an agent as a worklist; it never writes. planRepairs(root) folds the notebook (no index load, so it works where the keeper never started) and runs every NOTE_CHECKS entry whose noteTypes match each active note; repairWorklist(report) renders the self-describing page that CLI, MCP and all three slash commands share, so the instructions cannot be something only one wrapper says. Findings are grouped by check in NOTE_CHECKS order and each carries a ready kb write spec with the note id already filled in. It deliberately fixes NOTHING mechanically: an earlier version of this file DID fill anchor symbols from the keeper's sidecar, and its dry run proposed anchoring notes to root, out and opts — real declarations that are also ordinary prose.

summary: kb repair: detection worklist + the one mechanical exception, mechanicalSymbolRepair, which backfills anchors[].symbols on single-character file notes from the kb-notes-index sidecar (hub notes excluded, never overrides existing symbols, capped at SYMBOL_BACKFILL_CAP=15). Takes an optional preloadedSidecar so the keeper skips a redundant disk read. 2026-08-03: it can only ever fill the note's OWN anchor — the one whose path derives the note id (fileNoteId). It used to loop every anchor and re-put each under ITS own path; because kbWrite addresses a file note by spec.path, a secondary anchor's record landed on a different note, the real anchor stayed empty, and the pass re-fired every watcher cycle until the keeper's streak cap tripped and disabled auto-backfill permanently. It also now carries aliasesVerified forward when the note was already verified at its current edit, so a machine write does not push edits past aliasesVerifiedAtEdit and resurface the note in kb repair-aliases.
